page_title: How to make your own bittorrent client

summary.title: How to make your own bittorrent client
summary.one_liner: You learn how the BitTorrent protocol works by building a simple command-line BitTorrent client from scratch in Node.js, covering torrent parsing, UDP tracker communication, and peer downloads.
takeaways: A torrent client first gets a peer list by talking to a UDP tracker through a connect request followed by an announce request.
Torrent files are bencoded; the info dictionary is SHA1-hashed to produce the info hash that identifies the torrent.
Node.js buffers and writeUInt32BE/copy are used to build binary protocol messages byte by byte, with 64-bit values split into two 32-bit writes.
UDP suits tracker messages because they are small, while TCP is used for peer-to-peer file transfer; lost UDP messages are retried with exponential backoff.
summary.summary: This step-by-step tutorial builds a simple BitTorrent client in Node.js that can download the contents of a torrent file from the command line. It starts by reading and bencode-decoding a .torrent file, then covers the UDP tracker protocol, including building and parsing connect and announce messages with Node's dgram and Buffer APIs. The guide is organized as commits on a GitHub project, and the final section begins on downloading pieces from peers over TCP. It is aimed at JavaScript developers who want to learn backend networking and binary data handling.
